edition.authority: International Commission on English in the Liturgy Corporation, whose translation is reprinted; delivered by the Federation of Diocesan Liturgical Commissions with the approval of the Committee on Divine Worship of the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops
edition.jurisdiction: The universal ICEL English, common to ICEL's eleven member episcopal conferences. The FDLC is a United States body and the reprint is made under the USCCB's approval, but the text reprinted carries no national adaptation and is the universal ICEL English.
edition.notes:
A REPRINT, NOT THE MISSAL. The FDLC is the reprinter and not the rightsholder;
the English on every page is ICEL's approved translation of the Missale Romanum
2002/2008, reprinted under ICEL's standing permission for a free
non-commercial website. The leaflets carry no rubrics, no Order of Mass and no
apparatus of their own beyond the reflection beside each oration, and they must
never be cited as the Missal itself or as a ritual edition.

WHY THIS EDITION IS AN ACCEPTABLE EXEMPLAR. The maintainer has decided that the
FDLC reprint is an acceptable exemplar of ICEL's English: each oration is
reprinted whole, the acknowledgment on every page names ICEL as the
rightsholder, and the reprint is made with the approval of the USCCB's
Committee on Divine Worship. It is a second-tier exemplar -- the rightsholder's
own copy (ICEL's chant library) is the higher tier -- and it needs collating
rather than trusting: the Nineteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time Collect is
printed in one of these files as "Almighty every-living God" against the Latin
"Omnipotens sempiterne Deus", an evident typographical error in the reprint and
not a reading, and that slot was withheld from this harvest on that ground.

AS OF WHEN. The reprint is of the 2010 English and predates the May 2020
correction of the collect conclusions; the orations it prints end "one God, for
ever and ever" where the Missal now reads "God, for ever and ever". The
transcription carries what is printed and records the superseded reading where
it falls. No bytes are retained: the PDFs are remote and storage = remote.
edition.publication: A set of free PDF leaflets published by the Federation of Diocesan Liturgical Commissions at https://fdlc.org/ under "Mystagogical Reflections on Texts of the Roman Missal", each covering a span of Sundays and Solemnities and reprinting, for each, the Collect and the Prayer after Communion whole under the acknowledgment "Excerpt from The Roman Missal, Third Edition (c) 2010, ICEL. Reprinted with approval of the Committee on Divine Worship, United States Conference of Catholic Bishops." The files read in this lane were ComboColPaC78b_ORDINARY_Trin-13_SPI2016.pdf, ComboColPaC78c_ORDINARY_14-23_SPI2016.pdf, ComboColPaC78d_ORDINARY_24-30_SPI2016.pdf and ComboColPaC78e_ORDINARY_31-CTK_SPI2016.pdf; state retrieved 2026-08-21.

work.description: The Federation of Diocesan Liturgical Commissions' free online leaflets that reprint the Collect (and, in the 2016 series, the Prayer after Communion) of the Sundays and Solemnities of the Roman Missal whole, each beside a short mystagogical reflection, and each carrying the acknowledgment "Excerpt from The Roman Missal, Third Edition (c) 2010, ICEL. Reprinted with approval of the Committee on Divine Worship, United States Conference of Catholic Bishops." The English reprinted is ICEL's approved translation of the Missale Romanum 2002/2008; the FDLC is the reprinter and not the rightsholder. Registered because these leaflets are the only publicly reachable, exact copy of a large block of the Missal's orations in ICEL English, and the maintainer has accepted the FDLC reprint as an acceptable exemplar of that text.
